approval.notes: Approved as Sprint 4.5 (dedicated infra sprint before Sprint 5). The wiki inconsistency is a cross-cutting overhead on every sprint. 9 sprints remain — fixing now gives maximum ROI. No BA round-trip needed: technical scope is unambiguous.

content.tldr: Replace the fragile 60-file JSON wiki system with a single SQLite database (wiki.db) and an MCP server that lets AI agents read and write wiki state reliably — with transactions, schema enforcement, and full-text search. wiki-app refactored to read from SQLite directly.
content.problem_statement: The current wiki/ JSON system requires AI agents to manually update 5–8 files per action (feature status, dashboard, changelog, _index files). Files routinely fall out of sync because there are no transactions. JSON schemas in wiki/_schema/ exist but are never enforced at write time. buildSearchIndex() loops all files sequentially. Result: incorrect wiki state after nearly every sprint session.
content.solution_summary: SQLite database (wiki.db) as single source of truth. MCP server exposes structured tools for AI agents (wiki_dashboard, wiki_sprint_close, wiki_search, etc.). wiki-app refactored to query SQLite via better-sqlite3. JSON files become read-only exports for git snapshots.

actors.interaction: Calls MCP tools for all wiki reads/writes (replaces manual file editing)
Calls wiki_bug_create, wiki_bug_update, wiki_session_log MCP tools
Views wiki state via wiki-app — unchanged UX, consistent data

user_stories.story: As the project manager, I want to call wiki_sprint_close() once and have all 5 related records update atomically, so sprint closure never leaves the wiki in a partial state.
acceptance_criteria: wiki_sprint_close(id) updates sprint status, dashboard quick_facts, changelog, and feature statuses in a single SQL transaction
If any step fails, the entire transaction rolls back — no partial state
wiki_dashboard() reflects the closed sprint and new active sprint immediately after the call

user_stories.story: As the project manager, I want to call wiki_search('auth') and get matching features, bugs, and decisions ranked by relevance, so I can quickly orient to a topic without reading individual files.
acceptance_criteria: wiki_search returns results from features, bugs, decisions, api-contracts sections
Results include section, id, title, and a text snippet
Query uses SQLite FTS5 — results return in under 100ms

user_stories.story: As a developer, I want the wiki-app to show data that is always consistent with what AI agents wrote, so I can trust the wiki-app as the ground truth.
acceptance_criteria: wiki-app reads from wiki.db (not JSON files) via better-sqlite3 in server components
Any wiki_feature_update call is immediately visible in wiki-app on next page load
wiki-app build passes with 0 TypeScript errors after lib/wiki.ts → lib/db.ts refactor

user_stories.story: As QA, I want to call wiki_bug_create() and have the bug ID auto-assigned (BUG-XXXX), so I never have to manually look up the next bug number.
acceptance_criteria: wiki_bug_create auto-increments BUG-ID based on max existing ID in DB
Bug is immediately queryable via wiki_bug_list()
Severity and status are validated against allowed enums at insert time — invalid values rejected with clear error

business_rules: BR-WIKII-01: All wiki writes go through MCP tools after Sprint 4.5 — direct JSON file writes are deprecated
BR-WIKII-02: wiki.db is committed to git after each sprint session as the authoritative record
BR-WIKII-03: wiki_sprint_close and wiki_sprint_open are atomic — partial state is never persisted
BR-WIKII-04: All MCP write tools log to audit_log table with author, timestamp, and changed fields
BR-WIKII-05: wiki-app must not read JSON files after P2 complete — all reads go through better-sqlite3
BR-WIKII-06: SQLite WAL mode (PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL) enabled — allows concurrent reads from wiki-app while MCP writes

tasks.title: wiki-mcp/ scaffold — package.json, TypeScript config, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk + better-sqlite3 + zod, MCP server entry point with stdio transport
schema.sql — SQLite tables: features, sprints, tasks, api_contracts, bugs, history, decisions, changelog, audit_log + FTS5 virtual tables for features/bugs/decisions
migrate.ts — one-time JSON→SQLite importer, reads all wiki/ JSON files and populates DB idempotently (safe to re-run)
Core read tools — wiki_dashboard(), wiki_feature_get(id), wiki_feature_list(filters), wiki_sprint_get(id), wiki_bug_list(filters), wiki_contract_get(module)
Core write tools — wiki_feature_update(id, patch), wiki_task_update(id, patch), wiki_session_log(session)
Register MCP server in .claude/settings.json — mcpServers entry, command: node, args: [wiki-mcp/dist/server.js], auto-approve wiki_* tools
Composite atomic tools — wiki_sprint_close(id), wiki_sprint_open(id) — single transaction: sprint + dashboard + changelog + feature statuses
wiki_search(query, section?) — FTS5 full-text search across features/bugs/decisions/contracts — returns {section, id, title, snippet}
wiki_bug_create(data), wiki_bug_update(id, patch), wiki_bug_list(filters) — auto-increment BUG-ID, Zod enum validation on severity/status
wiki_contract_update(module, patch) — Zod validation of endpoint shape before insert, version auto-bump
Update vibe skill prompts — replace file-read patterns with MCP tool calls in vibe-project-manager, vibe-ba, vibe-qa-general skills
Add better-sqlite3 to wiki-app — server-side only, create lib/db.ts replacing lib/wiki.ts
Replace readWikiFile() calls in wiki-app page components with SQL queries via lib/db.ts
wiki-app admin API route — replace patchWikiFile() JSON write with SQL UPDATE via better-sqlite3

out_of_scope: Automatic audit trail triggers — manual logging in each tool for now
REST API for wiki — MCP stdio transport only
